v69_assumption: Illustration supplies a silent Herbal owner
exact_visible_reason: Each page is dominated by one continuous whole-plant construction, while prose occupies the residual spaces.
historical_calibration: Egerton MS 747 places large plant miniatures into the text area for a named substance; Egerton MS 2020 is a near-contemporary illustrated herbal.
v70_r2_revision: Retain WHOLE_PLANT as page owner, but do not promote any species name or treatment.

v69_assumption: Herbal pages are plant articles rather than process diagrams
exact_visible_reason: No pictured vessel, user, conduit, or operation touches any of the four plants.
historical_calibration: Illustrated herbals combine plant portrait and written properties/preparations without depicting every recipe action.
v70_r2_revision: Read the picture as an index/owner, not as a rebus for individual neighbouring cards.

v69_assumption: f10r is narrowly scabious or devil's-bit-like
exact_visible_reason: The broad repeated toothed leaves, blue radial head, outlined terminal form, and paired red underground swellings form no secure narrow match.
historical_calibration: Historical herbal traditions can stylize diagnostic parts, but genre resemblance is weaker than an identified specimen.
v70_r2_revision: Demote to BROAD_TOOTHED_COMPOSITE_FLOWERED_HERB; water preparation remains text-side invention.

v69_assumption: f11r is violet-like
exact_visible_reason: A dense rounded multi-axis crown with many repeated blue prongs and crossed tapering roots is unlike the minimal diagnostic structure expected from a narrow violet portrait.
historical_calibration: The Carrara Herbal explicitly contains an actual sweet-violet entry (Egerton 2020 f.94r), showing that violet was a nameable illustrated simple in this period; it does not make the Voynich image violet.
v70_r2_revision: Replace VIOLET with DENSE_BLUE_FLOWERED_CROWN_PLANT; keep violet only as a rejected comparison.

v69_assumption: f55v is Allium or plantain-like
exact_visible_reason: The enormous paired/fused leaf mass, branched apical spray, and animal-like irregular root do not cohere with a narrow Allium bulb/umbel or plantain rosette/spike.
historical_calibration: Medieval plant images may exaggerate roots or use memorable silhouettes, so grotesque form need not be literal zoology.
v70_r2_revision: Replace with BROAD_LEAF_PANICLED_PLANT_WITH_MNEMONIC_ROOT.

v69_assumption: f56r is sundew-like and supports a chest remedy
exact_visible_reason: The plant has two large spiny/rayed oval heads and a giant spiral/radial head on one tall branching axis; no small sticky-leaf rosette or pictured chest application appears.
historical_calibration: Herbal genre can carry remedies not pictured, but the image cannot select that species or ailment.
v70_r2_revision: Replace with MULTIHEAD_SPINY_OR_EMBLEMATIC_HERB; remove sundew and chest/h cough specifics from the live visual reading.

v69_assumption: Water may occur in a Herbal article even when not pictured
exact_visible_reason: No Herbal image shows water, but the picture can serve only as owner while prose carries preparation.
historical_calibration: Illustrated herbals describe medicinal preparations beyond what the single plant portrait depicts.
v70_r2_revision: Permit water only as an unbound recipe fill; do not treat any plant colour, swelling, or nearby card as WATER.

v69_assumption: Biological section is therapeutic balneology with an apparatus layer
exact_visible_reason: f81v shows many nude figures immersed to the waist in one bounded green field; f82r and f83r add cup/vessel stations and visibly joined arches/tubes.
historical_calibration: De balneis Puteolanis witnesses from the 13th–14th centuries and ca. 1400 explicitly depict nude bathers immersed in pools while discussing curative baths.
v70_r2_revision: Promote ILLUSTRATED_BALNEOLOGICAL_STATION_BOOK_WITH_APPARATUS_LAYER as R2's best content reading, without disease or body-part claims.

v69_assumption: Biological section is a purely impersonal waterworks manual
exact_visible_reason: Bodies and gestures are integral to every page, including the large shared enclosure and several terminal cups; they are not mere scale figures beside machines.
historical_calibration: Taccola's near-contemporary hydraulic drawings show that a true technical tradition existed, but its machine-centered purpose does not erase the Voynich figures.
v70_r2_revision: Retain bathhouse/apparatus operation as strongest rival, not as a sufficient whole-section explanation.

v69_assumption: Nude figures prove women's medicine or gynaecology
exact_visible_reason: Nudity, breasts, immersion, and repeated female-looking faces show a gendered pictorial vocabulary but no womb, birth scene, named illness, or diagnostic operation.
historical_calibration: De balneis imagery uses nude bathers for therapeutic waters without requiring a gynaecological genre; Morgan G.74 even uses male bathers.
v70_r2_revision: Remove women-specific diagnosis; allow female users, nymph/personifications, or workshop-standard figures.

v69_assumption: The six Bio records form continuous process cycles
exact_visible_reason: Several local assemblies are visibly disconnected: especially the two lower f83r systems and multiple f82r stations. Prose adjacency does not join them.
historical_calibration: Bath books commonly organize separate baths/virtues; technical notebooks likewise juxtapose independent devices.
v70_r2_revision: Prefer a catalogue of station-specific articles or variants over one manuscript-wide closed circulation cycle.

v69_assumption: Visible green in Bio is water
exact_visible_reason: Human lower bodies disappear into a bounded continuous green medium, making immersion much simpler than dry ground on these two pages.
historical_calibration: Medieval bath miniatures show bodies immersed in pools, though their pigment conventions vary.
v70_r2_revision: Use BATH_MEDIUM as image-near default, but keep GREEN_FILL in neutral data and do not infer chemical composition or flow.

v69_assumption: Conduits on f83r carry fluid in a known direction
exact_visible_reason: Contours genuinely connect vessels, cups, and a lobed terminal, but no arrows, level marks, or unambiguous source/sink signs choose direction.
historical_calibration: Early-fifteenth-century hydraulic manuscripts document siphons, pumps, mills, and water devices, but that historical possibility cannot supply absent arrows here.
v70_r2_revision: Retain CONNECTED_PATH and separate apparatuses; delete fixed feed/return direction from the revised unit.

v69_assumption: Text was fitted after images; line shape is often reflow
exact_visible_reason: Herbal prose occupies contour-shaped pockets; f82r/f83r lines bend around stations; circular writing follows diagram bands.
historical_calibration: Image-plus-text manuscripts routinely integrate figures in the text area; technical and astronomical codices also use local captions around diagrams.
v70_r2_revision: Strengthen image-first reflow. Do not convert line endings or image avoidance into semantic operators.

v69_assumption: Domain-neutral exemplar/card/register architecture
exact_visible_reason: Repeated local construction types and section-specific layouts suit exemplar copying, but the images do not show a codebook, four registers, or 14 controls.
historical_calibration: Illustrated herbal, bath, technical, and computistical manuscripts could all be copied by small workshops with exemplars.
v70_r2_revision: Retain only as production model; images add no evidence for exact card meanings or memory registers.

v69_assumption: f67r2 is simply a 7-by-12 selector
exact_visible_reason: The manifest image visibly contains two separate radial diagrams, each with its own centre and bands; neither is presented as an ordinary complete grid.
historical_calibration: Seven-planet by twelve-sign judgments are historically real, but can be tabular or disc-based; later Or 5591 explicitly preserves that relation.
v70_r2_revision: Rename TWO_RADIAL_CELESTIAL_REFERENCE_WHEELS; retain 7×12 only as a possible hidden inventory relation, not the visible page form.

v69_assumption: f68r1 is centre plus 28 spatial addresses
exact_visible_reason: That description fits part of the right circular panel but omits two open star fields and four additional face medallions across the foldout.
historical_calibration: Twenty-eight lunar segments could be organized in wheels, but star catalogues and calendars also use multiple panels.
v70_r2_revision: Rename MULTIPANEL_STAR_STATION_ATLAS_WITH_FIVE_FACE_CENTRES; no single sequence.

v69_assumption: f69v is one independent ordered 28-rule sequence
exact_visible_reason: Three disconnected rosette devices with different internal construction families are visible; each has a separate centre and text bands, and no common start or route is drawn.
historical_calibration: A mid-14th-century German book of fate uses 28 lunar segments and a wheel, proving the inventory is historically available, not that these three rosettes instantiate it.
v70_r2_revision: Replace with THREE_LOCAL_ROSETTE_LOOKUP_DEVICES; any total of 28 transcriptional loci remains a bookkeeping fact until visually bound.

v69_assumption: f68 and f69 have no licensed join
exact_visible_reason: No cross-page key, shared arrow, common start, or connector is visible; even within each foldout, major devices are disconnected.
historical_calibration: Independent calendrical, prognostic, and astronomical instruments often coexist in one codex; Add MS 82946 mixes moon tables, a wheel, Zodiac Man, and Blood-letting Man.
v70_r2_revision: Retain NO_VISIBLE_CROSSWALK, now strengthened by direct foldout inspection.

v69_assumption: Astro is specifically medical election practice
exact_visible_reason: Faces, stars, moon-like discs, wheels, and lookup geometry fit astronomical/astrological use, but no body map, operation picture, or treatment target appears in these three images.
historical_calibration: Add MS 82946 joins astronomical tables and an astrological wheel to Zodiac Man and Blood-letting Man around 1409–1431, showing genre coexistence, not identity.
v70_r2_revision: Keep IATROMATHEMATICAL_CALENDAR as one content expansion; generic calendar/prognostic/celestial atlas is equally strong or stronger visually.
